knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.6.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly defines a random sample from a population and why sampling precedes estimator construction?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the sampling warrant and inference ordering.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Random sample is about how data relate to a population model, not merely count or accidental equality of means. Estimators presuppose a sampling story.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Lawful draw from population model; observations alone are not enough.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Equating n observations with a random sample, or skipping the sampling warrant before estimators.

choices.label: A random sample is drawn so observations follow the population distribution under a stated sampling model (for example iid draws). Estimator and interval procedures require this warrant; a pile of observations is not automatically a random sample.
Any n observations collected in practice constitute a random sample because having data is sufficient for inference formulas to apply.
A random sample means the sample mean equals the population mean; once that equality holds, the sampling model is verified.
Sampling vocabulary is optional because estimator formulas can be applied to any spreadsheet column without a population model.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 2.6.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. An analyst takes the 40 most recent claims from one large commercial client and treats them as a random sample from the whole motor book. Which statement is correct?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Selection from one client breaks portfolio-level iid sampling. Large n, similar means, or deferred vocabulary do not repair the warrant.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Selection bias breaks random sample; n alone is insufficient.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Large-n rule, mean-match validation, or treating sampling as optional.

choices.label: Consecutive claims from one client are clustered and not an iid draw from the portfolio population; dependence and selection bias break the random-sample warrant. Having n = 40 observations does not by itself create a random sample.
Because n = 40 exceeds a common rule-of-thumb threshold, the extract is a random sample of the motor book regardless of how it was selected.
If the sample mean claim size is close to the book average, the selection mechanism is validated and the extract counts as a random sample.
Random-sample language applies only after an estimator is chosen; until then any claims file may be treated as a population draw.

worked_example.title: Classify a convenience extract as not a random sample
worked_example.problem_statement: An analyst pulls the 40 most recent claims from one large commercial client and treats them as a random sample from the whole motor book in order to build an estimator for portfolio mean severity. Decide whether this extract is a random sample from the stated population, and name the sampling defect.

given.value: 40 most recent claims, one commercial client

worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Compare the selection mechanism with an iid (or otherwise stated) draw from the motor-book population before judging the sample label.

steps.label: State what a random sample requires
steps.attempt_cue: Name the warrant that links observations to the population distribution.
steps.explanation: A random sample is drawn so that observations follow the population distribution under a stated sampling model (for example iid draws). Estimators and intervals inherit that warrant.
steps.calculation: Require: stated sampling model linking extract to motor-book population
steps.result: Random sample = lawful draw under a sampling model

steps.label: Inspect the actual selection mechanism
steps.attempt_cue: Describe how the 40 claims were chosen.
steps.explanation: The extract is consecutive recent claims from one client. That clusters time and client, so dependence and selection bias enter relative to the whole motor book.
steps.calculation: Mechanism = one-client recent slice (clustered, not portfolio iid)
steps.result: Selection is convenience / clustered, not portfolio random

steps.label: Classify and refuse n-as-warrant
steps.attempt_cue: Decide yes/no on random sample, and say why n = 40 alone fails.
steps.explanation: Having forty observations does not create a random sample. Without a lawful draw from the motor book, estimator procedures lack the sampling warrant.
steps.calculation: Classification: NOT a random sample from the motor book; defect = selection bias / clustering
steps.result: Not a random sample; n alone is insufficient

worked_example.final_answer: Not a random sample from the whole motor book: one-client consecutive claims are clustered and selection-biased. n = 40 does not by itself create a random sample.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Treating any large enough extract as a random sample because n = 40 looks adequate, without checking whether the draw matches the stated portfolio population.
